items.title: Every `[derive(..)]` over a struct (or enum) with a `<const N>` parameter fails: "in code generated by this attribute: `N` is a length parameter: give it a number or another length parameter, not the type `N`" - macro_std's `GenericParameter` carries no const flag, so `binders` spells `type N`
items.body: `[derive(PartialEq)] struct Buf<T, const N> { items: [T; N] }` (and Debug, Json, Default, Hashable alike) is refused inside the generated impl, because `derive_binders` (macro_std meta.vl) renders every generic as `type X[: Trait]` and the compiler's reflection of the generics does not say a parameter is a length. Fix: add `is_const: bool` to `GenericParameter` (the analyzer builds it at expansion time) and render `const N` in `derive_binders` and the bare name in `subject_spelling`; then pin one derive per trait over a `Buf<T, const N>`. Sizing S–M; lang-50 / the macro surface (not debug-50's files). Found probing E283's array half: a `[derive(Debug)]` over `[T; N]` is the natural use of the any-length impl.

items.title: Natively an array literal is emitted as `vec![..]` (a List) where its expected type is a fixed array `[T; n]` in two nested positions - a tuple slot of a struct-literal field or of a let used by a call, and a variant payload inside a list literal passed to `print` - so rustc refuses "expected `[i32; 3]`, found `Vec<i32>`"; JS is fine
items.body: Repros: `H { pair = ([5, 6, 7], true) }` with `pair: ([i32; 3], bool)`; `let t: ([i32; 2], bool) = ([1, 2], false); count(t)`; `print([Frame::Empty, Frame::Bytes([0, 0, 0, 1])])` with `Bytes([u8; 4])`. The same literals directly in a call argument or a lone variant constructor emit arrays correctly, so the expected type is lost one level inside a tuple or an element position (array-lengths S1's Type::Array(TypeId, TypeId) may have moved a path). Fix in vilan-rust's literal emission: thread the expected element/slot type through tuple, struct-field and list-element literals. Sizing S; vilan-rust.

items.title: Natively a struct with a `[|i32| i32; 2]` field (an array of closures) is refused by name ("does not emit a closure held inside `[Rc<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>; 2]`, which has no reference equality - `Option` and `List` of one do yet"), so `[derive(Debug)]` over it builds on JS only
items.body: `Option` and `List` of closures are admitted; a fixed array of closures is not. Probe: `struct Callbacks { fns: [|i32| i32; 2] }` with a `[derive(Debug)]` and `Callbacks { fns = [f, f] }.debug()`. Admit the array in the same check as List. Sizing S; vilan-rust.
